Greenways 
Grand Canal Greenway – Tullamore Urban 
The Part 8 for Grand Canal Greenway was 
published on the 14th of March; it 
encompasses a 2.8km section of the Grand 
Canal Greenway from Convent View, 
Tullamore to Srah Bridge, Ballydrohid, West 
of Tullamore.  This incorporates revisions to 
the previous Part 8 approved for the Grand 
Canal Greenway in 2015. The current 
proposal incorporates; 
1. Improvements 
to 
the 
existing 
towpath and footpaths along the 
Grand Canal through the provision of 
a suitable surface i.e. Surface 
Dressing, Asphalt Tarmac, Quarry 
Dust and Concrete / Stone Paving.  
2. Provision of traffic safety measures 
and 
signage 
to 
facilitate 
safe 
pedestrian and cycling crossings at 
Kilbeggan Bridge and Cox (Clara) 
Bridge (both protected structures). 
3. Provision of Shared Surface Area at 
Bury Quay and Offaly Street. 
4. Provision 
of 
access 
controls 
(pedestrian/cycling 
friendly 
gates/bollards) road makings, traffic 
calming measures facilitating the 
proposed cycle/walk way. 
5. Provision of a new pedestrian bridge 
at the 28th Lock, Srah, Tullamore.  
6. Information boards, street furniture, 
signage and lighting upgrades 
 
The Part 8 will be on public display from 
Thursday 13th of March 2019 to Thursday 
11th April 2019 and submissions can be 
made up until and including the 25th of 
April. Funding for this project has been 
approved under the Urban Regeneration 
Development Fund, 2018. Dept. of Housing, 
Planning and Local Government.

to  Kilbeggan

Water Quality 
The Local Authority Waters Programme 
hosted a Community Information Meeting in 
advance of any field work commencing in 
the River Gageborough Catchment. The 
meeting was held on Tuesday the 12th 
February last in the Streamstown/Horseleap 
Community Centre and informed all present 
of planned activities and assessments in the 
Gageborough Catchment. The meeting 
encouraged local input into the process.  
 
The Gageborough River is 1 of the 190 
Prioritised Areas for Action identified under 
the River Basin Management Plan for Ireland 
2018 -2021. It is an important source for 
drinking water in County Offaly. The river 
supplies Clara Water Treatment Plant where 
it is treated and distributed through a network 
of approximately 183km. 43 people from 
varying areas of interest attended the 
meeting, including pupils from the local 
school, 
tidy 
towns/community 
group, 
Teagasc 
and 
staff 
from 
Offaly 
and 
Westmeath County Councils.  The meeting 
was 
facilitated 
by 
Basil 
Mannion 
Community Water Officer for Offaly / 
Westmeath and members of the Catchment 
Assessment 
Team. 
The 
Catchment 
Assessment Team gave a presentation on 
how the catchment assessment/survey will 
be carried out. It is planned that work will 
commence once a suitable weather window 
permits.  The team also discussed challenges 
presented with existing known pressures 
within the catchment and the importance of 
improving the water quality status of both the 
Gageborough River and its tributaries. 
Active participation was encouraged through 
questions/answers and informal discussion.

Work has commenced on the kit-out of the 
new Tourist Office on O’Connor Square. It

open for business at Easter to greet the 
holiday season. A grant to the value of €20k

been

Offaly Tourism are currently seeking

Tourism Seminar 
Offaly County Council in association with 
Offaly Tourism Marketing (CLG) are 
hosting a Tourism Development Seminar on 
Monday, 8th April in The Tullamore Court

by

and 
networking 
opportunities.  It is hoped to be the first of a 
number of tourism networking events to be 
organised going forward. 
 
 
Holiday World Show 
‘Visit Offaly’ exhibited at the Holiday World 
Show in the RDS in Dublin on 25th, 26th & 
27th January. The largest and most 
successful holiday show the country; it was 
great exposure for our brand and product 
offering.  There was a genuine interest in 
what Offaly has to offer with visitors to the 
stand actively engaging in dialogue with the 
‘Visit Offaly’ team. We look forward to 
turning these potential opportunities into 
increased visitor numbers.

LOCAL ENTERPRISE OFFICE 
Launch of Midlands Regional Enterprise Plan 
to 2020 
On 6th February, The Minister for Business, 
Enterprise 
and 
Innovation 
Heather 
Humphreys TD, launched the first of nine 
new Regional Enterprise Plans to drive job 
creation and support enterprise growth in the 
regions. She was joined at the launch event 
in 
Mountmellick 
by 
Minister 
for 
Communications 
Climate 
Action 
and 
Environment, Richard Bruton TD, and 
Minister for Justice and Equality, Charlie 
Flanagan TD. 
 
The Regional Enterprise Plan for the 
Midlands 
identifies 
seven 
Strategic 
Objectives that build on the region’s 
strengths and address vulnerabilities that 
range from leveraging big data opportunities 
through the I-LOFAR telescope at Birr, to 
ensuring that the Midlands is well positioned

STREAM Creative Suite – Minister Heather 
Humphreys’ visit 
Following the launch of the Midland 
Regional Enterprise Plan to 2020 on 
February 6th 2019 in County Laois, Minister 
Humphreys travelled to Birr Castle to visit I-
LOFAR and the STREAM Creative Suite 
Project.  
Offaly Innovation & Design Centre CLG in 
partnership with Local Enterprise Office 
(LEO) Offaly, Offaly County Council and I-
LOFAR has been awarded €458,240 from 
the 
Enterprise 
Ireland 
Regional 
Development Fund to establish “STREAM 
Creative Suite” in Birr Technology Centre. 
Professor Peter Gallagher, Manager of the I-
LOFAR Consortium briefed the Minister and 
guests on I-LOFAR telescope. 
Orla Martin, Head of Enterprise in LEO 
Offaly explained that STREAM Creative 
Suite will be a natural extension to the I-
LOFAR Project. It will bring together 
researchers and practitioners in areas such as 
the visual arts, multi-media, technology 
and astronomy, 
who 
share 
a 
common interest in Big Data. 
Minister Heather Humphreys spoke of her 
delight “ to be here in Birr Castle to see first-
hand the work of I-LOFAR and the future 
plans for STREAM Creative Suite”. 
Offaly County Council Cathaoirleach Cllr. 
Danny Owens thanked Minister Humphreys 
and guests for taking the time to visit and he 
acknowledged the collaborative efforts those 
who made the successful application: Offaly 
County Council’s Chief Executive, Ms. 
Anna 
Marie 
Delaney; 
Head 
of 
Enterprise/Offaly Innovation & Design 
Centre CLG, Ms. Orla Martin; Prof. Peter 
Gallagher, I-LOFAR Consortium and Mr. 
Joe Hogan, Founder of Openet. 
 
LEO Offaly and Offaly County Council appear as 
Witnesses to the Oireachtas Joint Committee on 
Rural and Community Development.

now employs a team of nine professionals, 
delivering a suite of online software and 
related web services to over 300 clients 
throughout Ireland.

Edenderry based Derek McCreanor T/a 
Enhance Acoustics (Emerging Business 
Award); Ferbane based Ko Kombucha Ltd. 
(Artisan 
Food 
Business 
Award); 
Portarlington based Carla Mooney, Cardel 
Entertainment Ltd. (Female Entrepreneur 
Award) and Rahan based NIS Ltd. (Business 
Service Award).

Rise and Benefits of Remote Working Highlighted 
at Offaly Conference 
The benefits of remote working to both 
employers, employees and communities 
have been highlighted at a national 
conference in Tullamore on Friday last, 8th 
March.  The conference entitled “Remote 
Working 
– 
Practical 
Insights 
and 
Approaches” was organised by the Local 
Enterprise Office in Offaly in collaboration 
with The Junction Business Innovation 
Centre in Tullamore. The speakers at the 
Remote Working Conference were John 
Riordan of Shopify, Geraldine Beirne of 
LEO Offaly, Tracy Keogh of Grow Remote, 
Therese Philbin of AirBnB, Caroline Spollen 
of The Junction Offaly and Rory O'Keeffe of 
Hotjar. 
 
 
Set up and Grow a thriving Food Business in 
Ferbane 
LEO Offaly held a Food Event in Ferbane

event discussed Eco-friendly packaging, 
Food Technology & Regulation, financial 
advice and guest speaker Gerard Cleary CFO 
of Glenisk spoke of his experience growing 
Glenisk to be a multi-million euro business 
and national brand. 
 
 
Brexit and Beyond Event in Edenderry 
This event was being run in association with 
the Local Enterprise Office Offaly and the 
Edenderry & Local District Chamber of 
Commerce. Speakers at the event included 
James Maloney of Enterprise Ireland, 
Martina Keenan of Intertrade Ireland and 
Orla Martin of Local Enterprise Office. Lean 
expert Stuart Nelson of Jigsaw Consulting 
spoke about the benefits of using Lean 
techniques to save money, time and improve 
business performance. Eugene McNamara of 
Rosderra Meats shared their experience of 
adopting Lean strategies, and tips for other 
employers looking to do the same.

Bealtaine 2019 
The Library, Arts officer and the PPN officer

Bealtaine.  These events include the launch

Tullamore.  The Tovertafel is a fun care

late stage of their dementia journey with each 
other and with their surroundings, all the 
while stimulating movement. The beautiful 
games were developed specifically for the 
target group and can be played both 
independently and under supervision.

Lego workshops 
The success of the Brick.ie Lego exhibition 
in Birr Library has led to the development of 
staff run Lego workshops in Tullamore 
library.  This is a pilot and if successful will 
be introduced to the other libraries over time.  
There will be a series of 4 workshops on a
